name: Barbell Bench Press
why: The classic heavy chest press.
setup: Eyes under the bar, feet flat, shoulder blades pinched back.
Hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
form: Lower the bar to your mid chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the safety bars or use a spotter.
avoid: Bouncing the bar off your chest.
Elbows flared straight out to the sides.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

preferred.why: Main loadable chest press; bench strength is specific to the bench.

name: Wide-Grip Barbell Bench Press
why: Bench press with a wider grip: more chest, shorter path.
setup: Eyes under the bar, shoulder blades pinched back.
Hands well wider than your shoulders.
form: Lower the bar to your mid chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the safety bars or use a spotter.
avoid: Going so wide that your shoulders hurt.
Bouncing the bar off your chest.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
aliases: Barbell Incline Bench Press - Medium Grip
why: Heavy press for the upper chest.
setup: Bench at 30–45°, eyes under the bar.
Hands a bit wider than your shoulders, shoulder blades back.
form: Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: A lower incline keeps more of the work on the chest.
avoid: Bouncing the bar off your chest.
Lifting your hips off the bench.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

preferred.why: Heavy multi-joint press for the upper chest; strength is specific to the lift.

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
why: Bench press head-down: lower chest, shorter path.
setup: Decline bench, legs hooked in.
Hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
form: Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Have a spotter hand you the bar.
avoid: Bouncing the bar off your chest.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Wide-Grip Decline Barbell Bench Press
why: Decline press with a wide grip.
setup: Decline bench, legs hooked in.
Hands well wider than your shoulders.
form: Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Have a spotter hand you the bar.
avoid: Going so wide that your shoulders hurt.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
why: Flat press with a deeper stretch than the barbell.
setup: Lie flat, dumbbells over your chest, shoulder blades back.
form: Lower the dumbbells beside your chest, elbows angled in a little.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Go as deep as your shoulders allow.
avoid: Clanging the dumbbells together at the top.
Stopping short of the stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your chest

name: Neutral-Grip Dumbbell Bench Press
aliases: Dumbbell Bench Press with Neutral Grip
why: Flat dumbbell press, palms facing in: easier on the shoulders.
setup: Lie flat, palms facing each other, shoulder blades back.
form: Lower the dumbbells beside your chest, elbows close.
Press up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Stopping short of the stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your chest

name: One-arm Dumbbell Bench Press
why: Flat press one side at a time.
setup: Lie flat, one dumbbell over your chest.
Hold the bench with your free hand.
form: Lower the dumbbell beside your chest.
Press up until your arm is straight.
avoid: Twisting your body off the bench.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your chest

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
why: Upper chest press with a deep stretch.
setup: Bench at 30–45°, dumbbells over your upper chest.
Shoulder blades back.
form: Lower the dumbbells beside your upper chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: A lower incline keeps more of the work on the chest.
avoid: Stopping short of the stretch.
Arching off the bench.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your chest

preferred.why: Incline pressing grew the upper chest most in a trial; dumbbells add stretch.

name: Neutral-Grip Incline Dumbbell Press
aliases: Incline Dumbbell Bench With Palms Facing In
Hammer Grip Incline DB Bench Press
why: Incline dumbbell press, palms facing in: easier on the shoulders.
setup: Bench at 30–45°, palms facing each other.
form: Lower the dumbbells beside your upper chest, elbows close.
Press up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Stopping short of the stretch.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your chest

name: Decline Dumbbell Bench Press
why: Dumbbell press head-down, for the lower chest.
setup: Decline bench, legs hooked in, dumbbells over your chest.
form: Lower the dumbbells beside your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Sitting up fast at the end: you can get dizzy.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells beside your chest

name: Smith Machine Bench Press
why: Flat press on a fixed track: safe to push hard.
setup: Bench so the bar comes down on your mid chest.
Hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
form: Lower the bar to your mid chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the safety stops just below your chest.
avoid: Bench placed so the bar hits your neck or belly.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Smith Machine Incline Bench Press
why: Upper chest press on a fixed track.
setup: Bench at 30–45° so the bar comes down on your upper chest.
Hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
form: Lower the bar to your upper chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the safety stops just below your chest.
avoid: Bar landing on your neck.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Smith Machine Decline Press
why: Decline press on a fixed track.
setup: Decline bench under the bar, legs hooked in.
Hands a bit wider than your shoulders.
form: Lower the bar to your lower chest.
Press up until your arms are straight.
tips: Set the safety stops just below your chest.
avoid: Bouncing the bar off your chest.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → bar on your chest

name: Machine Chest Press
why: Stable chest press with steady tension: easy to push hard.
setup: Seat so the handles line up with your mid chest.
Back on the pad, shoulder blades back.
form: Push the handles out until your arms are straight.
Bring them back slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Shoulders rolling forward at the end.
Letting the stack slam between reps.
rangeOfMotion: Hands at your chest → arms straight

preferred.why: Top-rated chest exercise: deep stretch, steady tension, easy to add weight.

name: Incline Machine Chest Press
why: Upper chest press on a machine.
setup: Seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Back on the pad, shoulder blades back.
form: Push the handles up and out until your arms are straight.
Bring them back slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Shoulders rolling forward at the end.
rangeOfMotion: Hands at your chest → arms straight

name: Plate-loaded Chest Press
why: Plate-loaded chest press: heavy and stable.
setup: Seat so the handles line up with your mid chest.
Back on the pad, shoulder blades back.
form: Push the handles out until your arms are straight.
Bring them back slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Shoulders rolling forward at the end.
rangeOfMotion: Hands at your chest → arms straight

name: Plate-loaded Incline Chest Press
why: Plate-loaded press for the upper chest.
setup: Seat so the handles line up with your upper chest.
Back on the pad.
form: Push the handles up until your arms are straight.
Bring them back slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Shoulders rolling forward at the end.
rangeOfMotion: Hands at your chest → arms straight

name: Plate-loaded Decline Chest Press
why: Plate-loaded press angled down, for the lower chest.
setup: Seat so the handles line up with your lower chest.
Back on the pad.
form: Push the handles down and out until your arms are straight.
Bring them back slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Shoulders rolling forward at the end.
rangeOfMotion: Hands at your chest → arms straight

name: Seated Cable Chest Press
why: Chest press with cables: tension the whole way.
setup: Sit with your back on the pad, handles at chest height.
Elbows bent about 90°, shoulder blades back.
form: Press the handles forward and together, then pause.
Bring them back slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Letting the weights touch down between reps.
rangeOfMotion: Hands at your chest → arms straight
tempo: Push 1 s · Hold 1 s · Back 3 s

name: Incline Cable Chest Press
why: Cable press angled up, for the upper chest.
setup: Sit on an incline seat, handles at chest height.
Elbows bent about 90°, shoulder blades back.
form: Press up and together, then pause.
Bring the handles back slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Letting the weights touch down between reps.
rangeOfMotion: Hands at your chest → arms straight
tempo: Push 1 s · Hold 1 s · Back 3 s

name: Standing Cable Chest Press
why: Standing press with cables: tension the whole way.
setup: Pulleys at chest height, step a foot or two forward.
Staggered stance, elbows bent about 90°.
form: Press the handles forward and together, then pause.
Bring them back slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Leaning in to push with your body.
rangeOfMotion: Hands at your chest → arms straight
tempo: Push 1 s · Hold 1 s · Back 3 s

name: Push-Up
why: Bodyweight chest press, anywhere.
setup: Hands a bit wider than your shoulders, body straight.
form: Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Too easy? Add a plate on your back.
avoid: Hips sagging.
Half reps.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chest near the floor

name: Wide Push-Up
why: Push-up with wide hands: more chest.
setup: Hands well wider than your shoulders, body straight.
form: Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Hips sagging.
Half reps.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chest near the floor

name: Incline Push-Up
why: Easier push-up with hands up on a bench or bar.
setup: Hands on a bench or Smith bar, a bit wider than your shoulders.
Feet back, body straight.
form: Lower your chest to the bar.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Lower the bar to make it harder.
avoid: Hips sagging.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chest at the bar

name: Feet-Elevated Push-Up
why: Harder push-up with feet up: more upper chest.
setup: Feet on a bench, hands on the floor a bit wider than your shoulders.
Body straight.
form: Lower until your chest nearly touches the floor.
Push up until your arms are straight.
avoid: Hips sagging.
Half reps.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chest near the floor

name: Deficit Push-Up
why: Push-up with hands raised so the chest goes deeper.
setup: Hands on plates or push-up handles, a bit wider than your shoulders.
Body straight.
form: Lower until your chest is below your hands.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Too easy? Add a plate on your back.
avoid: Hips sagging.
Going deeper than your shoulders allow.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → chest below your hands

name: Chest Dip
why: Dip leaning forward: lower chest, deep stretch.
setup: Arms straight on the bars, lean forward, elbows out a little.
form: Lower until your shoulders are a bit below your elbows.
Push up until your arms are straight.
tips: Too easy? Add weight with a dip belt.
avoid: Dropping fast into the bottom.
Going deeper than your shoulders allow.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → shoulders below elbows

name: Dumbbell Fly
why: Chest stretched wide, no triceps.
setup: Lie flat, press the dumbbells up over your chest, palms facing in, elbows slightly bent.
form: Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a deep stretch.
Bring the dumbbells back together over your chest.
tips: Keep the same elbow bend the whole way.
avoid: Bending the elbows into a press.
Going so deep your shoulders hurt.
rangeOfMotion: Hands over your chest → arms wide

name: Incline Dumbbell Fly
aliases: Incline Dumbbell Flyes - With A Twist
why: Upper chest stretched wide.
setup: Bench at 30°. Press the dumbbells up over your upper chest, palms facing in, elbows slightly bent.
form: Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a deep stretch.
Bring the dumbbells back together over your upper chest.
avoid: Bending the elbows into a press.
Going so deep your shoulders hurt.
rangeOfMotion: Hands over your chest → arms wide

name: Decline Dumbbell Fly
why: Lower chest stretched wide.
setup: Decline bench, legs hooked in. Press the dumbbells up over your chest, palms facing in, elbows slightly bent.
form: Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a deep stretch.
Bring the dumbbells back together over your chest.
avoid: Bending the elbows into a press.
rangeOfMotion: Hands over your chest → arms wide

name: One-arm Dumbbell Fly
why: Fly one side at a time.
setup: Lie flat, hold the bench with your free hand.
Press the dumbbell up over your chest, elbow slightly bent.
form: Open your arm in a wide arc until you feel a deep stretch.
Bring the dumbbell back up over your chest.
avoid: Twisting your body off the bench.
rangeOfMotion: Hand over your chest → arm wide

name: Pec Deck
why: Machine fly: steady tension, easy to push hard.
setup: Seat so your arms are level with your shoulders.
Back flat on the pad.
form: Bring the handles together and squeeze 1 s.
Open slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Shoulders rolling forward.
Letting the stack slam between reps.
rangeOfMotion: Arms wide → hands together
tempo: In 1 s · Hold 1 s · Out 3 s

name: Cable Crossover
why: Standing cable fly from high pulleys, for the lower chest.
setup: Pulleys high, a handle in each hand, step forward.
Lean forward a little, elbows slightly bent.
form: Bring your hands together down in front of you and squeeze 1 s.
Open slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Bending the elbows into a press.
rangeOfMotion: Arms wide → hands together
tempo: In 1 s · Hold 1 s · Out 3 s

name: Low-to-High Cable Fly
why: Cable fly from low pulleys, for the upper chest.
setup: Pulleys low, a handle in each hand, step forward.
Arms down and out, palms forward.
form: Bring your hands up and together in front of your face and squeeze 1 s.
Lower slowly back out and down.
avoid: Shrugging your shoulders up.
Bending the elbows into a press.
rangeOfMotion: Arms low and wide → hands together at face height
tempo: In 1 s · Hold 1 s · Out 3 s

name: Single-arm Cable Crossover
why: Cable fly one arm at a time, across the body.
setup: Pulley high, handle in one hand, step forward.
Elbow slightly bent.
form: Bring your hand down and across your body and squeeze 1 s.
Open slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Twisting your body to move the weight.
rangeOfMotion: Arm wide → hand past the middle
tempo: In 1 s · Hold 1 s · Out 3 s

name: Lying Cable Fly
why: Flat fly with cables: tension at the top too.
setup: Flat bench between two low pulleys, chest in line with them.
Hands up over your chest, elbows slightly bent.
form: Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a deep stretch.
Bring your hands back together over your chest and squeeze 1 s.
avoid: Bending the elbows into a press.
rangeOfMotion: Hands over your chest → arms wide
tempo: Down 3 s · Up 1 s · Hold 1 s

name: Incline Cable Fly
why: Upper chest fly with cables.
setup: Incline bench at 30–45° between two low pulleys.
Hands up over your chest, elbows slightly bent.
form: Open your arms in a wide arc until you feel a deep stretch.
Bring your hands back together over your upper chest and squeeze 1 s.
avoid: Bending the elbows into a press.
rangeOfMotion: Hands over your chest → arms wide
tempo: Down 3 s · Up 1 s · Hold 1 s

name: Seated Cable Fly
why: Cable fly sitting tall: big stretch, steady tension.
setup: Bench upright between two pulleys at shoulder height.
Sit tall, arms open wide, elbows slightly bent.
form: Bring your hands together in front of your chest.
Open slowly until you feel a deep stretch.
avoid: Leaning forward off the bench.
Bending the elbows into a press.
rangeOfMotion: Arms wide → hands together

preferred.why: Top-rated chest exercise: loaded in the deep stretch, steady tension.

name: Cable Press-Around
why: One-arm cable move across the body: chest fully squeezed.
setup: Back to a high-ish pulley, handle in one hand.
Elbow bent, hand beside your chest.
form: Push your hand forward and across past the middle.
Return slowly until you feel a stretch.
avoid: Twisting your body to move the weight.
rangeOfMotion: Hand beside your chest → past the middle

name: Svend Press
why: Light chest finisher: press a plate out while squeezing it.
setup: Stand. Press a light plate (or two) between your palms at your chest.
form: Squeeze the plate and push it straight out until your arms are straight. Hold 1 s.
Bring it back to your chest slowly, still squeezing.
tips: A small plate keeps your hands close.
avoid: Letting the squeeze go.
Shrugging your shoulders.
rangeOfMotion: Plate at your chest → arms straight out
tempo: Push 1 s · Hold 1 s · Back 3 s

name: Dumbbell Squeeze Press
heavyWhy: pressing the dumbbells together limits the load
why: Dumbbell press with the bells pressed together: chest works the whole way.
setup: Lie on a flat bench, dumbbells touching over your chest, palms facing each other.
Arms straight.
form: Lower the dumbbells to your chest, pressing them together.
Press up, keeping them touching.
avoid: Dumbbells drifting apart.
Bouncing off your chest.
rangeOfMotion: Arms straight → dumbbells on your chest
